solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument's peg adjusted with skill once

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, as a tuning peg is adjusted

explanation.surface: A musician recalls tuning an instrument's peg with a skill they once had.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': Instrument is PEG SKILL ONCE rearranged. A peg suggests strings, but the answer has none.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Style of rap starts to generate almost overwhelming dread

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the outer letters wrap around the inner word
the starts of words are their first letters

parts.note: first letter of almost, still governed by 'starts to'

explanation.surface: A music critic says a style of rap tends to generate almost overwhelming dread.
explanation.walkthrough: The two starts sit either side of the dread, which they overwhelm.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the hip-hop genre built on street-crime themes.

clue.text: Chaps in team, number climbing on Scottish island above loch lacking depth

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it, so this comes first
in a down entry the island sits above the loch letter
the chaps go in the reversed team-and-number string, which holds them
in a down clue climbing means the team and number are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a side is a sports team
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides
L is the map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A team of men, with a number, climbs a hill on a Scottish island above a loch.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' and 'above' both mean the next piece comes lower down. Iona is a small island in the Hebrides, off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Something one-dimensional is shallow and flat, with no depth of character or complexity.

clue.text: King and leader of armada chat in boat

parts.note: K is the abbreviation for king, as in chess

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A monarch and a fleet's commander have a natter on a small vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a narrow covered canoe, so it is a type of small boat.

clue.text: Propose an item broadcast after drama

indicators.note: the scrambled letters come after the drama in the answer

parts.note: Noh (also spelt No) is classical Japanese drama

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these words' letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a news item be aired once the drama programme ends.
explanation.walkthrough: NO is the classical Japanese masked drama, usually spelt Noh.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate someone is to put them forward as a candidate, which is to propose them.

clue.text: Long stretch of trip in Europe

indicators.note: a stretch is a continuous run, here a run of letters lifted from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A long stretch of a trip spent in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the stretch, but it is the verb: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: pining and longing both mean yearning for something absent.

clue.text: Destroy order, losing time after time

indicators.note: 'after' in its sense of later in sequence: the shortened word follows

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to destroy an order, losing time again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' is not repetition: the first time is T, dropped from DICTATE, and the second is ERA, placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: eradicate literally means to pull out by the roots, hence to wipe out.

clue.text: Impure hero, sort mistakenly made head of religious community

indicators.note: done by mistake, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An impure hero of some sort is wrongly appointed to lead a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a scandal about a bad appointment; the unlikely hero becomes the nun in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the nun in charge of a convent, the religious community of the definition.

clue.text: Cross in past hour, upset, then relieved

indicators.note: then signals the next piece follows in order
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters of past and hour are read backwards

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by the house
to be rid of something is to be relieved of it

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy about the past hour finally feels relieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for angry, but here it is the noun: a mix of breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is a cross between two breeds, varieties or species, the offspring of mixed parents.

clue.text: Poor knight, feeble, wanting wife

indicators.note: 'wanting' cuts a letter off

explanation.surface: A poor, feeble knight who lacks a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is N in chess, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: lacking money or the necessities of life.

clue.text: Fellow attorney Conservative required

parts.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A notice that a fellow attorney who is a Conservative is required.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the American district attorney, and Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: demanded by law or rule, with no choice about it.

clue.text: Putting arachnid in pipe?

indicators.note: 'in' places one word inside the other

parts.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice; the arachnid goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are putting a spider in a tobacco pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' reads as a tube, but it is the verb, to sing shrilly.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense: 'stick it in the drawer' uses the verb to mean place.

clue.text: Reflected on hard image in code

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone reflected on a hard-to-read image hidden in a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected on' looks like 'thought about', but it splits: reflected is the reversal and on is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a system for disguising a message by swapping its letters.

clue.text: Story from a relative omitting one gripping point

indicators.note: to grip is to hold tight, so the outer letters hold the inner word

parts.note: a dot is a point, gripped by the rest

explanation.surface: A story told by a relative who leaves out one gripping point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' reads as exciting, but it means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short, entertaining account of a real incident.

clue.text: Dreadful in operation, ignoring first in command

explanation.surface: Something dreadful in a military operation, ignoring the first in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in command' looks like a phrase, but 'first' belongs to the deletion and 'in' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an official instruction issued by an authority.

clue.text: Holy ship's company mostly in blue

indicators.note: 'in' places the shortened word inside the next

parts.note: blue = sad, holding the shortened crew

explanation.surface: A holy ship's crew, most of them feeling blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is the mood, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: set apart for, or connected with, God or religion.

clue.text: Area guarded by soldier perhaps on border, a thing that's abhorred

indicators.note: guards stand around what they guard, so the letter is surrounded by the next word
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the border

parts.note: a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: An area guarded by a soldier on the border, something everyone hates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier perhaps' signals an example: a soldier ant, not a soldier. The 'a' after the comma looks like part of the definition, but it is the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something utterly detested, originally a thing cursed by the Church.

clue.text: Walk out on expanse of land without water

definitions.meaning: abandon a person or post: the verb, stressed on the second syllable
an arid region such as the Sahara: the noun, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone walks out on to a dry expanse of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently but spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: one spelling for both abandoning someone and a barren, arid region.

clue.text: Reject racket broken by seed

indicators.note: something broken is split open, here to let the other word in

parts.note: a din is a racket, split open
to seed a field is to sow it

explanation.surface: A tennis player rejects a racket after being broken by a seeded opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all tennis: racket, broken, seed. None of it survives: the racket is noise and the seed is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to refuse to acknowledge someone as your own.

clue.text: Anxious at home with scoundrel coming into view

indicators.note: 'with' means together with, so the parts are set side by side

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: to come into a place is to enter it, so one word enters the other

parts.note: to view is to see, taking in the scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious at home as a scoundrel comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming into view' reads as appearing, but it splits: 'coming into' is the container and 'view' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacking confidence and uneasy.

clue.text: Dean set to work in part of London

indicators.note: to work material is to knead it into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean is set to start a job in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'set to work' reads as one phrase; only 'to work' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the traditionally working-class district east of the City of London.

clue.text: Put a stop to school hosting business account finally

indicators.note: hosting means the school abbreviation holds the next letters inside it as guests

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of account

explanation.surface: A school shuts down a commercial account it had been running.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a rumour or plan is to end it decisively, to crush or quash it.

clue.text: Beginners lead rest astray

parts.note: the lead in a show is its star

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters of rest are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: An instruction to a guide to take novices off the beaten path, leaving everyone else lost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a verb but is the noun: a lead actor is the STAR. 'astray' scrambles REST into TERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Starters are those just setting out on something, the same idea as novices or beginners.

clue.text: Bird that's black and yellow, not caught

indicators.note: 'not caught' asks for the word without the cricket scorer's letter for caught

parts.note: yellow in its sense of cowardly, which is craven

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher describes a black and yellow bird that got away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black and yellow' reads as a bird's plumage, but yellow means cowardly. C is the cricket abbreviation for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A description by example: the large glossy corvid whose plumage is jet black.

clue.text: Mere share

definitions.meaning: a mere is a small lake
the verb, as when resources are put together for common use

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' reads as 'only', but it is the noun: a small lake, common in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a small lake, and to combine resources for common use.

clue.text: Boring sport, one followed by a few

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the next part is placed behind

parts.note: to sport a hat is to wear it

explanation.surface: A spectator finds a sport dull, with one player followed by a few others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a game, but it is the verb: to sport clothes is to have them on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: so tedious that it wears you out.

clue.text: Weakness about love, say

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around, so the outer word goes round the letter

parts.note: a vice is a moral weakness, placed around O

explanation.surface: A confession of weakness about love, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the noun: to have a say.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: having a say in something is having an opinion that counts.

clue.text: Revolutionary behind lines, protected by new name, unusually polite

indicators.note: behind means this piece comes after the rest in the answer
something protected by another is shielded inside it, so one piece goes inside the other
unusually signals the letters of new name are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so LL is lines
a revolutionary is a red, a radical left-winger

explanation.surface: A radical hiding behind enemy lines under a fresh alias turns out to be oddly courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' looks like part of the definition but rearranges NEW NAME into WEMANNE; 'protected by' wraps that round the lines, and 'behind' adds the revolutionary at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with good manners behaves courteously, which is what being polite means.
